author: Alex Kienlen
title: Arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin announces $18.4 million settlement against lease-to-own firm - NewsBreak
text:
By Alex Kienlen ,
1 hours ago
LITTLE ROCK, Ark. – Arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin said on Wednesday that Arkansans are eligible for a financial settlement of more than $18 million.
Griffin said the settlement with the lease-to-own firm Snap Financial covers anyone who did business with the firm from 2017 to 2022 and cancels $18,449,844 in lease payments. This will affect more than 9,300 Arkansans, he said.
Arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin announces $32 to $80 million settlement over PCB environmental contamination claims The Arkansas settlement is a share of the $664 million settlement between Snap and 16 other attorneys general.
Officials said Snap Finance offers lease-to-own agreements through retail partners, buying merchandise from retailers and leasing it to consumers. A multistate investigation found the company allegedly used misleading disclosures, failed to provide complete contract terms before signing, and made it difficult for customers to return products or end leases.
States alleged that some consumers believed they were agreeing to short-term payment plans but instead entered into longer, more expensive leases. Investigators also said Snap misled some customers into believing its program could improve their credit scores and examined the company's debt collection and lease-termination practices.
Maynard woman gets 7-year sentence for abusing an adult she was caring for Under the settlement, Snap agreed to stop using potentially misleading advertising, provide full lease disclosures before contracts are signed, clarify repair and replacement responsibilities, and stop threatening repossession when it does not intend to reclaim merchandise. The company must also clearly explain consumers' rights to terminate leases, provide practical return options, pause charges while it processes termination requests, and submit annual compliance reports for three years.
“Misleading agreements that leave consumers paying far more than they expected are unacceptable” Griffin said. “This settlement provides meaningful financial relief to more than 9,300 Arkansans and holds Snap Finance accountable for its deceptive business practices.”
Arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin sues OpenAI over safety of ChatGPT The settlement includes more than $662.1 million in lease forgiveness for consumers and a $2.75 million payment to participating states, including $150,000 for Arkansas. Arkansas joined the Iowa- and Nebraska-led settlement, along with 14 other states.
